gadm_units.description: GADM 4.1 states and districts, the candidates of the locality reconciliation service at /-/reconcile/gadm, with a point-radius georeference (centre and uncertainty radius) and a simplified outline (geometry) for display.

gadm_adm_0.description: GADM 4.1 country at full resolution, used by spatial queries. Hidden from the table list because its map would download several MB; gadm_units has simplified outlines for display.

gadm_adm_1.description: GADM 4.1 states at full resolution, used by spatial queries. Hidden from the table list because its map would download several MB; gadm_units has simplified outlines for display.

gadm_adm_2.description: GADM 4.1 districts at full resolution, used by spatial queries. Hidden from the table list because its map would download several MB; gadm_units has simplified outlines for display.

admin_unit_georeference.title: Georeference to a state or district (point-radius)
admin_unit_georeference.description: Give a coordinate and uncertainty radius for a specimen whose locality can only be placed in a state or district, using the point-radius method: the centre of the unit (its centroid, or a point inside it when the centroid falls outside, e.g. for crescent shapes or island groups) and the distance from that centre to the furthest point of the unit's boundary. Parameters: admin1 - the state (old and variant names such as Malacca, Johore, Penang, North Borneo are recognised); admin2 - the district, optional; when given, the district is georeferenced, otherwise the whole state. Returns one row per matching unit: lat/lon (WGS84 decimal degrees), uncertainty_radius_m, area_km2 and how the centre was chosen. Boundaries are GADM 4.1 (present-day units), so a historical unit may not match its modern namesake.
admin_unit_georeference.sql:
WITH p AS (
    SELECT trim(:admin1) AS a1,
           trim(replace(replace(trim(:admin2), 'Daerah ', ''), ' District', ''))
               AS a2
),
unit AS (
    SELECT 'district' AS level, d.NAME_2 AS name, d.NAME_1 AS admin1_name,
           d.geometry
    FROM gadm_adm_2 AS d
    JOIN gadm_adm_1 AS s ON s.NAME_1 = d.NAME_1, p
    WHERE p.a2 <> ''
      AND (d.NAME_2 LIKE p.a2 OR '|' || d.VARNAME_2 LIKE '%|' || p.a2 || '%')
      AND (p.a1 = '' OR s.NAME_1 LIKE p.a1
           OR '|' || s.VARNAME_1 LIKE '%|' || p.a1 || '%')
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'state', s.NAME_1, s.NAME_1, s.geometry
    FROM gadm_adm_1 AS s, p
    WHERE p.a2 = '' AND p.a1 <> ''
      AND (s.NAME_1 LIKE p.a1 OR '|' || s.VARNAME_1 LIKE '%|' || p.a1 || '%')
),
centred AS (
    SELECT level, name, admin1_name,
           ST_Contains(geometry, ST_Centroid(geometry)) AS centroid_inside,
           CASE WHEN ST_Contains(geometry, ST_Centroid(geometry))
                THEN ST_Centroid(geometry)
                ELSE ST_PointOnSurface(geometry) END AS c,
           ST_Area(geometry, 1) / 1e6 AS area_km2,
           -- The furthest boundary point from any centre is a hull vertex
           ST_DissolvePoints(ST_ConvexHull(geometry)) AS hull
    FROM unit
),
hull_points(level, name, admin1_name, centroid_inside, c, area_km2, hull, i, n) AS (
    SELECT level, name, admin1_name, centroid_inside, c, area_km2, hull,
           1, ST_NumGeometries(hull)
    FROM centred
    UNION ALL
    SELECT level, name, admin1_name, centroid_inside, c, area_km2, hull, i + 1, n
    FROM hull_points
    WHERE i < n
)
SELECT level,
       name,
       admin1_name,
       round(Y(c), 5) AS lat,
       round(X(c), 5) AS lon,
       CAST(max(ST_Distance(c, GeometryN(hull, i), 1)) AS INTEGER) + 1
           AS uncertainty_radius_m,
       round(area_km2, 1) AS area_km2,
       CASE WHEN centroid_inside THEN 'centroid'
            ELSE 'point inside unit (centroid falls outside)' END AS centre_method,
       'WGS84' AS datum,
       'point-radius; GADM 4.1 boundaries' AS method
FROM hull_points
GROUP BY level, name, admin1_name
ORDER BY level, admin1_name, name

find_place.title: Find a place by name
find_place.description: Look up gazetteer places by name, matching the official name, the ASCII name and all alternate names (including historical and variant spellings), case-insensitively. Parameter: name - the place name as written on a specimen label, or the start of one (e.g. "Bukit Ti" matches "Bukit Timah"). Exact matches are returned first (match_type 'exact'), then names that start with the text ('prefix'), most populous first. matched_name is the name variant that matched. total_matches counts all matching places, of which at most 50 are returned: if it is more than 1, the name is ambiguous and the state, district or feature type on the label is needed to choose. lat/lon are WGS84 decimal degrees.
find_place.sql:
WITH matches AS (
    SELECT geonameid,
           min(CASE WHEN name = trim(:name) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS prefix_only,
           substr(min(CASE WHEN name = trim(:name) THEN '0' ELSE '1' END || name), 2)
               AS matched_name
    FROM geonames_names
    WHERE trim(:name) <> ''
      AND name >= trim(:name)
      AND name < trim(:name) || char(1114111)
    GROUP BY geonameid
)
SELECT g.geonameid,
       g.name,
       round(g.latitude, 5) AS lat,
       round(g.longitude, 5) AS lon,
       g.feature_class,
       g.feature_code,
       fc.description AS feature,
       a1.name AS admin1_name,
       a2.name AS admin2_name,
       nullif(g.population, 0) AS population,
       coalesce(nullif(g.elevation, ''), nullif(g.dem, '')) AS elevation_m,
       m.matched_name,
       CASE m.prefix_only WHEN 0 THEN 'exact' ELSE 'prefix' END AS match_type,
       count(*) OVER () AS total_matches
FROM matches AS m
JOIN geonames AS g USING (geonameid)
LEFT JOIN feature_codes AS fc ON fc.code = g.feature_code
LEFT JOIN admin_1_codes AS a1 ON a1.code = g.admin1_code
LEFT JOIN admin_2_codes AS a2 ON a2.code = g.admin2_code
ORDER BY m.prefix_only, g.population DESC, g.name
LIMIT 50

reconcile_locality.title: Reconcile a locality to a GADM state or district
reconcile_locality.description: Suggest the GADM state or district that a verbatim specimen label locality lies in, e.g. "Kg. Sg. Rengit, Kota Tinggi" or "10 mi S of Kuala Lumpur". This is the same scoring as the OpenRefine reconciliation service: every run of one to six words is looked up in the gazetteer (with label abbreviations such as Kg., Sg., Bt., Mt. expanded), and offsets such as "10 km N of X" are projected from X. Parameters: locality - the locality text as written; admin1 (optional) - the state as written on the label, old names such as Johore or Malacca accepted; admin2 (optional) - the district as written. Returns up to 25 candidates, best first. score (0-100) is the percentage of the evidence in the text consistent with the unit; is_match is 1 only when the top candidate is well supported and clearly ahead of the rest. evidence lists the names that supported each candidate: read it before accepting one. When is_match is 0, check the place names with find_place, or a coordinate with reverse_geocode. lat/lon is the unit's centre and uncertainty_m the radius of a point-radius georeference for the whole unit. No rows means no known place names were found.
reconcile_locality.sql:
SELECT json_extract(j.value, '$.id') AS gid,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.name') AS name,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.type[0].id') AS unit_type,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.score') AS score,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.match') AS is_match,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.description') AS evidence,
       u.admin1_name,
       u.lat,
       u.lon,
       u.uncertainty_m
FROM json_each(reconcile_locality(:locality, nullif(trim(:admin1), ''),
                                  nullif(trim(:admin2), ''))) AS j
JOIN gadm_units AS u ON u.gid = json_extract(j.value, '$.id')
ORDER BY j.key

reverse_geocode.title: Describe a coordinate (reverse geocode)
reverse_geocode.description: Describe where a point is: the country, state and district boundaries (GADM) that contain it, and the 10 nearest gazetteer places within about 50 km, each with its distance and the compass direction from the place to the point. Use it to check a specimen's coordinates against its label, or to write a locality description. Parameters: lat, lon - WGS84 decimal degrees; feature_classes - optional comma-separated GeoNames feature classes to limit the nearby places to (P populated places, H streams/lakes, T mountains/hills, L areas, S spots/buildings/ estates, V forest, R roads, A administrative); leave empty for all. Rows with kind 'country'/'state'/'district' are the containing boundaries; rows with kind 'nearby' are places, nearest first, with a ready-made locality phrase such as "3.2 km NE of Kampung X".
reverse_geocode.sql:
WITH pt AS (
    SELECT MakePoint(CAST(:lon AS REAL), CAST(:lat AS REAL), 4326) AS g
),
admin AS (
    SELECT 1 AS sort, 'country' AS kind, NULL AS geonameid, a.COUNTRY AS name,
           NULL AS feature_code, 'country' AS feature,
           NULL AS admin1_name, NULL AS admin2_name
    FROM gadm_adm_0 AS a, pt
    WHERE MbrContains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1 AND ST_Contains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2, 'state', NULL, a.NAME_1, NULL, lower(a.ENGTYPE_1), a.NAME_1, NULL
    FROM gadm_adm_1 AS a, pt
    WHERE MbrContains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1 AND ST_Contains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 3, 'district', NULL, a.NAME_2, NULL, lower(a.ENGTYPE_2), a.NAME_1, a.NAME_2
    FROM gadm_adm_2 AS a, pt
    WHERE MbrContains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1 AND ST_Contains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1
),
nearby AS (
    SELECT g.geonameid, g.name, g.feature_code, g.latitude, g.longitude,
           g.admin1_code, g.admin2_code,
           ST_Distance(g.geom, pt.g, 1) AS distance_m,
           Degrees(Azimuth(g.geom, pt.g)) AS azimuth
    FROM geonames AS g, pt
    WHERE g.rowid IN (
        SELECT rowid FROM SpatialIndex
        WHERE f_table_name = 'geonames' AND f_geometry_column = 'geom'
          AND search_frame = BuildCircleMbr(
              CAST(:lon AS REAL), CAST(:lat AS REAL), 0.5, 4326)
    )
    AND (trim(:feature_classes) = ''
         OR instr(',' || upper(replace(:feature_classes, ' ', '')) || ',',
                  ',' || g.feature_class || ',') > 0)
    ORDER BY distance_m
    LIMIT 10
),
nearby_described AS (
    SELECT n.*,
           CASE WHEN n.distance_m < 50 THEN ''
                ELSE trim(substr(
                    'N  NNENE ENEE  ESESE SSES  SSWSW WSWW  WNWNW NNW',
                    (CAST((n.azimuth + 360 + 11.25) / 22.5 AS INTEGER) % 16) * 3 + 1,
                    3))
           END AS direction
    FROM nearby AS n
)
SELECT kind, geonameid, name, feature_code, feature, admin1_name, admin2_name,
       lat, lon, distance_m, direction, locality
FROM (
    SELECT sort, kind, geonameid, name, feature_code, feature,
           admin1_name, admin2_name,
           NULL AS lat, NULL AS lon, NULL AS distance_m, NULL AS direction,
           NULL AS locality
    FROM admin
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 4, 'nearby', n.geonameid, n.name, n.feature_code, fc.description,
           a1.name, a2.name,
           round(n.latitude, 5), round(n.longitude, 5),
           CAST(round(n.distance_m) AS INTEGER),
           n.direction,
           CASE WHEN n.direction = '' THEN 'at ' || n.name
                ELSE printf('%.1f km %s of %s', n.distance_m / 1000.0,
                            n.direction, n.name)
           END
    FROM nearby_described AS n
    LEFT JOIN feature_codes AS fc ON fc.code = n.feature_code
    LEFT JOIN admin_1_codes AS a1 ON a1.code = n.admin1_code
    LEFT JOIN admin_2_codes AS a2 ON a2.code = n.admin2_code
)
ORDER BY sort, distance_m

validate_coordinates.title: Check coordinates against the stated state and district
validate_coordinates.description: Check whether a specimen's coordinates fall inside the state (admin1) and district (admin2) written on its label, and test the common transcription errors. Parameters: lat, lon - WGS84 decimal degrees as recorded; admin1 - the state on the label (old and variant names such as Malacca, Johore, Penang, North Borneo are recognised); admin2 - the district, optional. Returns one row per hypothesis: 'as given', then latitude/longitude swapped, and each sign flipped. For each: the state and district the point actually falls in, whether that matches the label (1/0, or null when no name was given or it was not recognised), the distance in km to the stated unit (0 when inside), and an assessment. stated_admin1_matched/stated_admin2_matched show which boundaries the label names were matched to. If 'as given' does not match but a swapped/flipped row does, the record probably has that error.
validate_coordinates.sql:
WITH p AS (
    SELECT CAST(:lat AS REAL) AS lat,
           CAST(:lon AS REAL) AS lon,
           trim(:admin1) AS a1,
           trim(replace(replace(trim(:admin2), 'Daerah ', ''), ' District', ''))
               AS a2
),
stated1 AS (
    SELECT s.NAME_1, s.geometry
    FROM gadm_adm_1 AS s, p
    WHERE p.a1 <> ''
      AND (s.NAME_1 LIKE p.a1 OR '|' || s.VARNAME_1 LIKE '%|' || p.a1 || '%')
),
stated2 AS (
    SELECT d.NAME_1, d.NAME_2, d.geometry
    FROM gadm_adm_2 AS d, p
    WHERE p.a2 <> ''
      AND (d.NAME_2 LIKE p.a2 OR '|' || d.VARNAME_2 LIKE '%|' || p.a2 || '%')
      AND (NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated1)
           OR d.NAME_1 IN (SELECT NAME_1 FROM stated1))
),
variants(sort, variant, lat, lon) AS (
    SELECT 1, 'as given', lat, lon FROM p
    UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'latitude and longitude swapped', lon, lat FROM p
    UNION ALL SELECT 3, 'latitude sign flipped', -lat, lon FROM p
    UNION ALL SELECT 4, 'longitude sign flipped', lat, -lon FROM p
    UNION ALL SELECT 5, 'both signs flipped', -lat, -lon FROM p
),
points AS (
    SELECT v.*,
           CASE WHEN v.lat BETWEEN -90 AND 90 AND v.lon BETWEEN -180 AND 180
                THEN MakePoint(v.lon, v.lat, 4326) END AS g
    FROM variants AS v
),
checked AS (
    SELECT pt.sort, pt.variant, pt.lat, pt.lon, pt.g,
           (SELECT a.COUNTRY FROM gadm_adm_0 AS a
            WHERE MbrContains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1 AND ST_Contains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1)
               AS country,
           (SELECT a.NAME_1 FROM gadm_adm_1 AS a
            WHERE MbrContains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1 AND ST_Contains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1)
               AS found_admin1,
           (SELECT a.NAME_2 FROM gadm_adm_2 AS a
            WHERE MbrContains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1 AND ST_Contains(a.geometry, pt.g) = 1)
               AS found_admin2,
           CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated1) OR pt.g IS NULL THEN NULL
                ELSE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated1 AS s
                             WHERE MbrContains(s.geometry, pt.g) = 1
                               AND ST_Contains(s.geometry, pt.g) = 1)
           END AS in_stated_admin1,
           CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated2) OR pt.g IS NULL THEN NULL
                ELSE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated2 AS s
                             WHERE MbrContains(s.geometry, pt.g) = 1
                               AND ST_Contains(s.geometry, pt.g) = 1)
           END AS in_stated_admin2
    FROM points AS pt
),
measured AS (
    SELECT c.*,
           CASE WHEN c.in_stated_admin1 = 1 THEN 0
                WHEN c.in_stated_admin1 = 0 THEN
                    (SELECT min(ST_Distance(s.geometry, c.g, 1)) FROM stated1 AS s) / 1000.0
           END AS km_from_stated_admin1,
           CASE WHEN c.in_stated_admin2 = 1 THEN 0
                WHEN c.in_stated_admin2 = 0 THEN
                    (SELECT min(ST_Distance(s.geometry, c.g, 1)) FROM stated2 AS s) / 1000.0
           END AS km_from_stated_admin2
    FROM checked AS c
)
SELECT m.variant,
       round(m.lat, 5) AS lat,
       round(m.lon, 5) AS lon,
       m.country,
       m.found_admin1,
       m.found_admin2,
       (SELECT group_concat(NAME_1, '; ') FROM stated1) AS stated_admin1_matched,
       (SELECT group_concat(NAME_2 || ' (' || NAME_1 || ')', '; ') FROM stated2)
           AS stated_admin2_matched,
       m.in_stated_admin1,
       m.in_stated_admin2,
       round(m.km_from_stated_admin1, 1) AS km_from_stated_admin1,
       round(m.km_from_stated_admin2, 1) AS km_from_stated_admin2,
       CASE
           WHEN m.g IS NULL THEN 'not a valid coordinate'
           WHEN m.country IS NULL THEN 'outside the country'
           WHEN p.a1 <> '' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated1)
               THEN 'stated state not recognised; found in ' || coalesce(m.found_admin1, '?')
           WHEN m.in_stated_admin1 = 0
               THEN printf('not in stated state (%.1f km away)', m.km_from_stated_admin1)
           WHEN p.a2 <> '' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stated2)
               THEN 'in stated state; stated district not recognised'
           WHEN m.in_stated_admin2 = 0
               THEN printf('in stated state but not in stated district (%.1f km away)',
                           m.km_from_stated_admin2)
           WHEN m.in_stated_admin2 = 1 THEN 'consistent with stated state and district'
           WHEN m.in_stated_admin1 = 1 THEN 'consistent with stated state'
           ELSE 'in ' || coalesce(m.found_admin1, '?')
       END AS assessment
FROM measured AS m, p
ORDER BY m.sort

locality-reconcile.service_name: Geonomia: GADM state or district from a locality description
